extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in vision-language/video question answering and multimodal machine learning (esp. those studying humor, creativity, and magic in videos)
extracted.subtask_description: Design and evaluation of video question-answering tasks and dataset construction specifically for counter-intuitive / surprising videos (humor, creative performances, magic) to test spatial-temporal reasoning, description, and counter-intuitiveness reasoning in VLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive Timestamp Localization Task
rubrics_metrics.description: The localization task involves localizing counter-intuitive segments within the video, answers expressed in either seconds or frames. It is the base task to assess the model’s comprehension abilities and serves as the basis for subsequent tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires understanding the video’s overall content, incorporating both temporal and spatial information. Answers must be numeric timestamps (seconds or frames). Anti-pattern: models that only describe video content rather than providing the specific time period. Empirical note: no model currently can reliably solve this task; models tend to produce descriptive outputs instead of timestamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed Description Task
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate coherent and objective free-text descriptions of the selected moment in the video to evaluate information extraction and fundamental video understanding capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers are free-text and substantially longer than typical VideoQA datasets (FunQA average answer length 34.2 words). This task is used to analyze how a model extracts information and produces text for downstream reasoning tasks. Static-frame approaches are insufficient — temporal dynamics must be captured. Evaluated with NLG metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT) and semantic metrics (GPT-4 scoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitiveness Reasoning Task
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate concrete free-text explanations of why the video is surprising (e.g., Why Humorous, Why Creative, Why counter-intuitive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a difficult task requiring deep reasoning using information from the entire video plus common-sense knowledge. The task assesses models’ ability to reason about violations of expectation and to articulate the comedic/creative/magical cause. Evaluated with the same set of NLG and semantic metrics; requires whole-video integration rather than single-frame analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title Task
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher-level task (for HumorQA and CreativeQA) requiring generation of a concise title summarizing the video’s content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should be concise and vivid, capturing the main surprising/creative element. This is treated as a higher-level inference task beyond description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Scoring Task
rubrics_metrics.description: In CreativeQA, rate the creativity of videos on a numeric scale between 1 and 20 (provided officially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplies a quantitative, human-judged creativity score for model evaluation. Annotators provide official scores; models are evaluated on how well they predict or align with these scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magic Method Task
rubrics_metrics.description: In MagicQA, explain clearly the rationale behind the magic (how the effect is achieved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This task tests deeper causal and mechanism reasoning. To ensure accuracy, this task is only partially annotated and appears only in the test set (see appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual-centered and Counter-intuitive Reasoning Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA design principle: dataset is visual-centered and emphasizes counter-intuitive reasoning and spatial-temporal reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset collection and annotation prioritize visual cues over audio; ablation experiments show muting audio minimally affects evaluation scores, emphasizing the visual-centric nature. Models should focus on visual evidence and temporal relationships to detect counter-intuitive elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on Temporal Dynamics (not static frames)
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA requires strong emphasis on temporal dynamics rather than solely on few frames of images; many QAs cannot be answered from static frames alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human experiment: sampling 8 evenly spaced frames was insufficient for 86% of participants to answer counter-intuitive questions. Models must capture sequence, causality, repetition, and timing to succeed (e.g., humor often depends on repeated events or contrast over time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-text long-answer format
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA uses free-text QA with long responses (average 34.2 words) to increase the demand for advanced video comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished from 'open-ended' short answers in other datasets. Metric evaluation should handle long-form natural language generation; semantic metrics (e.g., GPT-4 based) are emphasized because n-gram metrics may fail to reflect semantic correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation Quality Control: multi-person, multi-round review
rubrics_metrics.description: Every annotation included in the final release undergoes rigorous multi-person, multi-round review processes, including training and screening of annotators and secondary cross-validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A random 10% of tasks were re-reviewed for consensus evaluation. Consensus categories: High (consistent understanding), Medium (partial agreement), Low (disagreement). Empirical target: ≈91% High consensus, ≈1% Low consensus. Annotation originally in Chinese, then translated and expanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus Evaluation (High/Medium/Low)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotator agreement is categorized into High, Medium, and Low consensus to measure objectivity and reliability of annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in quality control; report: across a 10% sample, 91% High, 8% Medium, 1% Low. Use consensus statistics to judge dataset reliability and to guide selection/curation of samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset Construction Pipeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline comprises Pre-processing (crawling, cleaning, cutting, exclude non-ethical and sensitive content), Manual Annotation (in Chinese with trained annotators), and Post-Processing (automatic translation and augmentation using GPT-3.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual cleaning to ensure counter-intuitive features and quality; training/screening annotators; second-round checks on 10% of tasks; post-process includes translation and synthetic QA generation faithful to original ideas to expand to multilingual dataset and increase QA count. Follow ethical filtering and maintain test set secrecy to avoid leakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset Subset Specifications (HumorQA, CreativeQA, MagicQA)
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA contains three subsets: HumorQA (1,769 web videos, avg length 7s), CreativeQA (927 videos from Kasou Taishou, avg 48s), MagicQA (1,672 magic videos of various genres).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each subset targets different types of counter-intuitiveness (humor: incongruity/contrast; creative: imitation and props; magic: illusions and transformations) and includes tailored tasks (H1-4, C1-5, M1-3). Use subset-specific tasks and evaluation strategies because distributional properties (length, effect types) differ significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, WUPS, GPT-4 based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a mix of traditional NLG metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, CIDEr), learned semantic metrics (BLEURT), lexical/semantic similarity like WUPS, and LLM-based evaluation (GPT-4 scoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/limits: WUPS is unreliable for sentence-level or phrase answers and can be misleading (produces high scores for semantically wrong but lexically related words). GPT-4 provides stronger semantic judgments but can be unstable (recommend multiple runs and averaging). Choose metrics mindful of their biases for long free-text answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure-mode awareness (models often fail on spatial-temporal reasoning and timestamp localization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed model failures: models describe content rather than provide timestamps; fail to track sequential events and causal relationships; poor performance on explanation/reasoning tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use failure analyses to prioritize temporal modeling, integration of common-sense knowledge, and sequence-level reasoning. Timestamp localization requires models to emit numeric intervals rather than descriptive text. Consider multi-turn or coaching agents (e.g., FunMentor) to guide VLMs toward better reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive task design: Perceive -> Articulate -> Reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks are structured to progressively assess perception, articulation, and reasoning about counter-intuitive elements: 1) localization (perceive when), 2) description (articulate what), 3) reasoning (explain why).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluation and model training curricula to follow this progression to isolate which stage a model fails on and to scaffold learning from detection to explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset augmentation and derived task variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-processing created additional sub-datasets: FunQA-MC (multiple choice), FunQA-DIA (dialogue QA), and FunQA-MC-R (multi-choice version specifically containing counter-intuitive reasoning questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These derived versions allow testing different model interfaces and settings (classification vs generation, dialogue multi-turn). When using augmented data, track provenance (human vs GPT-generated) and avoid contamination of test splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and sensitive-content filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: During pre-processing, exclude non-ethical and sensitive content to ensure dataset appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curators must screen and cut videos to avoid harmful, non-consensual, or sensitive material. Maintain documentation of filtering criteria and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human baseline evaluation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Human performance measured by selecting random QA pairs and collecting multiple human answers, then evaluating with the same metrics as models (BLEU-4 / ROUGE-L / CIDEr / BLEURT / GPT-4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple human annotators (e.g., 5) and average results to obtain reliable human baselines. Compare model vs human scores to quantify the gap and to set meaningful targets for model improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to protect test set and avoid data leakage
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure fair comparisons and prevent data leakage, future research is advised not to utilize the FunQA testing set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building models or augmenting data, strictly separate training/validation/test splits and document any external pretraining data that may overlap with FunQA test clips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations to consider (scope of annotations and translation artifacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current dataset primarily contains video-level data and annotations (not dense object/temporal/object-level annotation); initial annotations were in Chinese and later translated to English, which may introduce cultural or translation differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful when interpreting cross-lingual annotations; consider extending dataset with denser annotations (object-level, finer temporal annotations) and examining cultural biases in humor/creativity judgments when training or evaluating models.

rubrics_metrics.name: FunMentor: multi-turn dialogue agent design
rubrics_metrics.description: FunMentor is proposed as an agent that uses multi-turn dialogues to enhance VLMs’ understanding of counter-intuitiveness, operating like a seasoned coach to steer model responses toward fluent, logical, and persuasive explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-turn guidance to refine model outputs, supply prompts that scaffold reasoning, and iteratively elicit deeper explanations. FunMentor showed empirical effectiveness in experiments and can be used as a methodological approach to improve counter-intuitive reasoning.
